entries.status: FDA-approved Oct 15, 2004 as an in-hospital bridge to transplant (PMA P030011). BiVACOR's titanium maglev heart is in an early feasibility trial.
entries.bottleneck: Durability, external driver/power, clotting and infection
entries.goal: BiVACOR goal: transplant-bridge approval as early as late 2027 (company goal)

entries.status: A pig lung worked in a brain-dead human for 216 hours (Nature Medicine, Aug 2025). No living-human trials found.
Gene-edited pig kidneys in living patients through UT's EXPAND trial and eGenesis expanded access. UCSF's implantable bioartificial kidney is still lab-stage.
entries.bottleneck: Rejection and immunosuppression; pig virus monitoring
entries.goal: UT goal: commercial no later than 2030 (company goal)

entries.status: First auxiliary pig liver in a living recipient, May 2024 (patient died on day 171). A 1-patient ex-vivo pig-liver perfusion trial is running.

The first FDA-approved 'artificial pancreas' was the MiniMed 670G in Sep 2016. Automated insulin delivery is now sold by Medtronic, Tandem and Insulet. Vertex's zimislecel stem-cell islets are in a pivotal study.
entries.bottleneck: External pump and sensor; cell therapy needs immunosuppression

entries.example: PSYONIC Ability Hand; Open Bionics Hero; Esper Hand
entries.status: Muscle-controlled bionic hands are on sale, and PSYONIC adds touch feedback. Atom Limbs' Atom Touch is waitlist-only.
entries.bottleneck: Noisy surface EMG, few degrees of freedom, socket comfort, insurance

entries.example: Össur Power Knee; Ottobock Genium; MIT nerve-controlled leg (AMI)
entries.status: Microprocessor and powered knees are on sale. MIT's nerve-controlled bionic leg reached near-natural walking speed (Nature Medicine, Jul 2024).
entries.goal: MIT team goal: commercial in about 5 years, so ~2029 (team goal)

entries.status: CE-marked and launched in Europe on Jul 22, 2026 for geographic atrophy (dry AMD). Still investigational in the US.
entries.bottleneck: Low resolution; fits only certain causes of blindness

entries.example: Cochlear Ltd, Advanced Bionics, MED-EL cochlear implants
entries.status: FDA-approved since 1984. About 736,900 devices implanted worldwide as of Dec 2019 (NIDCD).
entries.bottleneck: Music and noisy rooms; external processor

entries.status: Lab-grown denovoSkin is in a Phase 3 trial for burns. Electronic 'bionic skin' has been shown only in rats.
entries.bottleneck: Sensor density vs. real skin; touch needs nerve electrodes

entries.status: FDA-approved Dec 19, 2024 as the first acellular tissue-engineered vessel, for limb artery trauma. A coronary bypass version has an accepted IND.
entries.bottleneck: Small vessels clot; capillary networks inside organs

entries.example: Integrum OPRA bone-anchored implant; iSens (Case Western)
entries.status: The OPRA bone-anchored leg system was FDA-approved in Dec 2020. Implanted 2-way nerve interfaces like iSens are in first-in-human studies.
entries.bottleneck: Channel count, infection, wireless power, recalibration

entries.status: First human bladder transplant May 4, 2025 (with a kidney, from a deceased donor). The patient had full function at 1 year, and a second patient has been transplanted. I found no verified artificial or bioengineered bladder in human use.
entries.bottleneck: Lifelong immunosuppression; no artificial bladder yet

entries.status: Several CT-based custom titanium implants got FDA 510(k) clearance, and 3D-printed spinal cages are on sale. These replace defects, not whole bones.

entries.example: Stryker Mako, Zimmer Biomet, Smith+Nephew robotic knee replacement
entries.status: Joint replacement is routine. Robot-assisted knees were 16% of US primary knee replacements in 2024 (AJRR).
entries.bottleneck: Implants wear out; cartilage barely regrows

entries.example: University of Tokyo / Waseda biohybrid hand
entries.status: A lab-grown muscle hand fatigues after about 10 minutes. MIT's fatigue-resistant myoneural actuator has been tested only in rodents (2026).
